'Corl-shades' is asymmetric..why: Everything is made up: the relation and both lattices. All names are absent from Dolma and from a web search. ("outweaves", the first name, was dropped: it is a real English verb, "to surpass in weaving", whose meaning already implies asymmetry.)

sources.note: No use of the verb; hits were coral colour palettes and window shades.
No lattice of either name; hits were arctic-curve lattice papers and lattice-structure patents.

notes: Fictional all: a made-up relation between made-up lattices. Asymmetry added; direct no (asked as 'can the second corl-shade the first?'), d1 no, d2 yes. d1's 'no' is also the asymmetric conclusion, so unlike the other 'no' queries the edit makes it a firm no rather than merely 'does not follow'; it is still marked discriminates: false because the pre-edit answer is also no. RBox: the instance facts are in the prompt, so each 'Does it follow ...?' query is determinate by construction (no determinacy, no worlds). A 'no' answer (the conclusion does not follow) is the same before and after the insert, since nothing follows about a made-up relation before it, so those queries carry discriminates: false; they are there to keep yes and no balanced (CRITERIA Rule 9) and to catch over-generalization of the inserted property. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
